summary: CUPS is a print management system built in C that relies on the Internet Printing Protocol to handle output jobs. It acts as the underlying service on Unix-like environments to route documents between local machines and networked printing hardware.
goodFor: This is a suitable choice if you manage a traditional Unix-like network and need a standardised mechanism to queue and dispatch print jobs.
watchOut: Configuring the underlying driver rules and network queues can involve complex troubleshooting, and legacy endpoints can expose security vulnerabilities if left unpatched.
deployNotes: As a compiled C application, it typically runs directly on the host system as a persistent background daemon without requiring a separate database.
